version.changelog:
- Added support for signature keys and access control (ACL) policies, including create/list/delete actions.
- Introduced three new analyze actions, including policy effect diagnosis.
- Expanded managed and query action set from 17 to 24 operations; SKILL.md and acceptance criteria updated to reflect full API coverage.
- Integrated skill-quality-cli for all CLI commands; every hcloud call now runs via quality telemetry wrapper (enforced in workflow, new scripts added).
- Updated dependencies and installation flow: added ensure_cli.sh, removed legacy/informal SDK and skill-card.md files.
- Improved documentation for prerequisites, critical warnings, and workflow; clarified unsupported features and stricter trigger keywords.

llm.summary: The APIG management instructions are mostly coherent, but the skill mandates a persistent telemetry wrapper that can send unredacted cloud command output and local agent session metadata to a remote service.

dimensions.detail: The reporting code reads Huawei-related credentials from environment variables to authenticate reporting, posts telemetry to Huawei quality endpoints or a guest endpoint, and can include APIG responses such as signature-key creation output.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The installer writes a reusable executable and Python sources under ~/.local/bin and appends PATH exports to ~/.bashrc and ~/.profile. The bundled installer is local/offline, but cli_entry.py also contains manual install/upgrade paths that download packages from a remote endpoint.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires every hcloud command to use the wrapper; the documentation discloses automatic quality telemetry and an opt-out variable, but does not clearly disclose that successful command stdout up to 6000 characters is reported.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No service, scheduler, or privilege escalation was found, but the wrapper persists across shell sessions and the reporting module reads local opencode, hermes, codex, and ai-shell session identifiers or agent metadata when explicit values are absent.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated APIG management purpose is real and includes confirmation rules for mutating and delete operations, but the bundled skill-quality-cli adds a generic command wrapper and default remote reporting that is broader than APIG management.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review carefully before installing. Use a least-privilege Huawei Cloud account, avoid running secret-returning operations through the telemetry wrapper, set SKILL_QUALITY_REPORT=0 if you do not want reporting, and be aware that installation modifies shell startup files and leaves a persistent wrapper in ~/.local/bin.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Verified: the mandatory run wrapper captures subprocess stdout and reports output_result without redaction; this is disproportionate for APIG administration because command output may include sensitive cloud data.
[TT3] unexpected: Partly verified: reporting intentionally uses network sinks and Huawei credentials for telemetry. The IAM-token path appears aimed at Huawei authentication, but the guest endpoint is only checked with startswith("http") and telemetry payloads can include sensitive command output.
[TP4] unexpected: Verified as a Review concern, not tool poisoning by itself: ensure_cli.sh persists a wrapper in ~/.local/bin and modifies shell startup files, which is broader than a normal APIG command guide.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Verified: the package contains substantial installer/reporting/session-discovery code in addition to APIG instructions, and that code is not necessary for the declared APIG operations.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Verified: skill-quality-cli run is a generic subprocess wrapper. Passing command arguments as a list avoids basic shell injection, but the wrapper still executes arbitrary supplied commands and reports their outputs by default.
[E2] expected: Downgraded in part: dict(os.environ) is used to pass the current environment to the child process and add SKILL_TRACE_ID, not to transmit the full environment. The remaining credential concern comes from explicit reporting credential reads.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Verified: comments claim host session-store collection was removed, but later code falls back to collect_session_id_only() and collect_agent_only(). The inactive ensure_latest code is less material because main does not call it automatically.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Verified: default telemetry can send stdout, error summaries, input parameters, and local session or agent metadata without just-in-time user consent.
[SQP-3] unexpected: The language/locale observation is not material to the verdict, but the contradictory privacy comments about session-store access are material under-disclosure.
[YR1] unexpected: Downgraded from malware-signature framing: the matched lines are PATH persistence in shell profiles, not a backdoor payload, but they still support the persistence concern.
[LP3] unexpected: Verified: the skill does not declare a narrow permission/tool scope despite requiring shell execution, local writes, environment access, cloud credentials, and network reporting.
[AST4] unexpected: Verified: subprocess.run is central to the telemetry wrapper; it is not shell-injection evidence by itself, but it expands the skill into a broad command execution and reporting mechanism.
